name: Adamus Perseniae
pdTranslations: Letters excerpted with English translation in medieval anthologies
modernTranslations: The Book of Mutual Love (Washington and Lee University thesis/dissertation)
untranslatedHighlights: Mariale (12 Marian sermons) - translated to French (R. Thomas 1963) but not comprehensive English

name: Hugo de Folieto
modernTranslations: The Medieval Book of Birds: Hugh of Fouilloy's Aviarium (Willene B. Clark, 1992, Medieval & Renaissance Texts and Studies vol. 80)
untranslatedHighlights: De claustro animae (On the Cloister of the Soul), De medicina animae, and other moral treatises remain primarily in Latin

name: Joannes Damascenus
pdTranslations: Exposition of the Orthodox Faith - multiple 19th-c. translations
modernTranslations: Writings (Fathers of the Church 37, trans. Frederic H. Chase, Catholic University of America Press 1958); Three Treatises on the Divine Images (trans. Andrew Louth); On the Orthodox Faith (St. Vladimir's Seminary Press recent translation)
untranslatedHighlights: None - comprehensively translated (note: PL entry is a Latin version of a Greek author)

name: Auctor incertus (Liutprandus Cremonensis?)
pdTranslations: Genuine Liudprand works translated by F. A. Wright (1930)
modernTranslations: If genuinely Liudprand: The Complete Works of Liudprand of Cremona (trans. Paolo Squatriti, CUA Press 2007) covers the authentic corpus; works marked incertus likely fall outside it
untranslatedHighlights: Attribution unclear - dubious/spurious works attributed to Liutprand of Cremona; marked incertus

name: Paulus S. Petri Carnotensis
modernTranslations: Only scholarly excerpts translated in academic works; no full translation
untranslatedHighlights: Paul, monk-treasurer of Saint-Pere de Chartres, compiler of the cartulary (Vetus Agano, 1066-1088); critical edition by Guerard (1840) is Latin/French, no English translation

name: Reinerus S. Laurentii Leodiensis
modernTranslations: None located despite works in Patrologia Latina and MGH
untranslatedHighlights: 16 works including theological, exegetical, controversial, historical, biographical and hagiographical writings

name: Sugerius S. Dionysii
modernTranslations: Abbot Suger on the Abbey Church of St.-Denis and Its Art Treasures (Erwin Panofsky ed./trans., 1946); Selected Works of Abbot Suger (Richard Cusimano & Eric Whitmore)
untranslatedHighlights: Some minor works may not be fully covered in Panofsky edition

name: Petrus Vallis Cernaii
modernTranslations: The History of the Albigensian Crusade: Peter of Les Vaux-De-Cernay's Historia Albigensis (W. A. Sibly & M. D. Sibly, Boydell and Brewer 1998)
untranslatedHighlights: None - primary work fully translated

name: Paulinus Aquileiensis
modernTranslations: None located
untranslatedHighlights: Liber exhortationis (Liber de salutaribus documentis) - first 'mirror for princes' - remains in Latin (PL 99:197-282)

name: Theodulfus Aurelianensis
pdTranslations: Hymn translations in English hymnals (Gloria, laus et honor as 'All Glory, Laud and Honor')
modernTranslations: The Poetry of Theodulf of Orleans: A Translation and Critical Study (Nikolai A. Alexandrenko, Tulane dissertation 1970)
untranslatedHighlights: Prose works (De Spiritu Sancto) remain primarily untranslated

name: Vigilius papa
modernTranslations: Selected letters translated in Orthodox Christian Theology publications and Roman Letters project
untranslatedHighlights: Complete epistolary corpus not fully translated; many letters remain in Latin

name: Paulus Vinfridus
pdTranslations: History of the Langobards (William Dudley Foulke 1907, University of Pennsylvania)
modernTranslations: Multiple modern editions and translations; also known as Paul the Deacon (Paulus Diaconus)
untranslatedHighlights: Some minor works (homilies, poems) less covered; Historia Langobardorum comprehensively translated

name: Notkerus Balbulus
pdTranslations: 1867 translation in Bibliotheca rerum germanicarum vol. 4
modernTranslations: Two Lives of Charlemagne: Einhard and Notker the Stammerer (trans. Lewis Thorpe 1969)
untranslatedHighlights: Gesta Caroli translated; hymns, sequences and other liturgical works remain partially untranslated

name: Joannes Belethus
modernTranslations: None located
untranslatedHighlights: Summa de ecclesiasticis officiis (Rationale divinorum officiorum) - German translation (Weinrich, CCT 11) but no English

name: Lupus Ferrariensis
modernTranslations: The Letters of Lupus of Ferrieres (trans. Graydon W. Regenos 1966)
untranslatedHighlights: None - 132 surviving letters translated

name: Oddo Astensis
modernTranslations: None located
untranslatedHighlights: Expositio in Psalmos (dedicated to Bruno of Asti/Segni, PL 165) remains untranslated in Latin

name: Jacobus Caietanus
modernTranslations: None located
untranslatedHighlights: Giacomo Gaetani Stefaneschi's Opus Metricum (verse life of Celestine V, the earliest biography of the hermit-pope) has no identified English translation

name: Smithius, Joannes
modernTranslations: Not applicable
untranslatedHighlights: John Smith (18th-c. editor of Bede): Annotationes in operibus Bedae, printed in PL 95 - modern editorial apparatus in Latin, not a medieval authorial corpus; not a realistic translation target

name: Paulus Alvarus Cordubensis
modernTranslations: The Indiculus luminosus of Paul Alvarus (trans. Kenneth Baxter Wolf, Translated Texts for Historians 84)
untranslatedHighlights: Letters and Vita Eulogii less certain; major work fully translated

name: Gaufridus Claraevallensis
modernTranslations: The First Life of Bernard of Clairvaux (trans. Hilary Costello OCSO, Cistercian Fathers Series 76); Geoffrey's section of Vita Prima included
untranslatedHighlights: Some shorter works may remain untranslated

name: Heterius Uxamensis
modernTranslations: None located; Latin critical edition in Corpus Christianorum (1984) with French introduction
untranslatedHighlights: Adversus Elipandum libri duo (with Beatus of Liebana) - key anti-adoptionist work of 8th-c. Spain remains untranslated

name: Anselmus Havelbergensis
modernTranslations: Anticimenon: On the Unity of the Faith and the Controversies with the Greeks (trans. Ambrose Criste OPraem & Carol Neel, Cistercian Studies Series 232/Premonstratensian Texts and Studies)
untranslatedHighlights: Some minor writings may not be fully covered

name: Arnulfus Lexoviensis
modernTranslations: None located
untranslatedHighlights: Works in PL 201 - primarily letters and other ecclesiastical writings remain in Latin

name: Hormisdas I
modernTranslations: Pope Hormisdas Letters 77 & 80 (trans. John Collorafi); Formula of Hormisdas widely translated; scattered translations in patristic anthologies
untranslatedHighlights: Complete epistolary collection not comprehensively translated

name: Marcellus Memorialis
modernTranslations: The Conference of Carthage in 411 (trans. Erika Hermanowicz & Neil McLynn, Translated Texts for Historians 90, Liverpool University Press) - first English translation of the Gesta collationis Carthaginiensis, the 411 Catholic-Donatist conference transcript recorded under the notary Marcellus
untranslatedHighlights: None - the conference transcript now fully translated

name: Udalricus Cluniacensis
modernTranslations: A Medieval Latin Death Ritual: The Monastic Customaries of Bernard and Ulrich of Cluny (trans. Therese Schroeder-Sheker, Studies in Music-Thanatology 1, 1993); dedicatory epistle and proemium edited/translated by S. Boynton and I. Cochelin
untranslatedHighlights: Full Antiquiores consuetudines cluniacensis monasterii not comprehensively translated to English

name: Baldricus Dolensis
modernTranslations: Baldric of Bourgueil, 'History of the Jerusalemites': A Translation of the Historia Ierosolimitana (trans. Susan B. Edgington, intro. Steven J. Biddlecombe, Boydell Press 2020) - first English translation of his First Crusade history
untranslatedHighlights: Poems, saints' lives and other of the 7 PL works remain untranslated; major work (Historia Ierosolimitana) now fully translated

name: Alexander S. Augustini Cantuariensis
modernTranslations: Only selected chapters translated informally (e.g., Gregory Sadler's translations of Dicta Anselmi chapters); Latin critical text in Memorials of Saint Anselm (ed. Southern & Schmitt)
untranslatedHighlights: Dicta Anselmi (sayings of Anselm recorded by the monk Alexander of Canterbury) - no complete English translation

name: Hieronymus Radiolensis
modernTranslations: No translations located
untranslatedHighlights: Girolamo da Raggiolo (Italian, d. ca. 1515) - very limited bibliographic information available; only a bare Wikidata entry found

name: Godefridus Viterbiensis
modernTranslations: None located
untranslatedHighlights: Pantheon and Chronicon - chronicles of world history to 1186 - remain in Latin

name: Ulfilas Moeso-Gothorum
pdTranslations: The First Germanic Bible: Translated From The Greek By The Gothic Bishop Wulfila In The Fourth Century (ed. Gerhard Hubert Balg 1891)
modernTranslations: Multiple modern editions of Gothic Bible; scholarly treatments in German and English
untranslatedHighlights: None significant - the work is itself a Bible translation; Gothic text with apparatus widely available

name: Lambertus Hersfeldensis
modernTranslations: The Annals of Lampert of Hersfeld (trans. I.S. Robinson, Manchester Medieval Sources Series 2015)
untranslatedHighlights: None - Annales fully translated

name: Remigius Lugdunensis
modernTranslations: Predestination-controversy texts partially accessible via Gottschalk and a Medieval Predestination Controversy: Texts Translated from the Latin (Genke & Gumerlock, Marquette 2010), but the Lyon dossier attributed to Remigius (De tribus epistolis, attribution contested with Florus/Ebbo) not fully translated
untranslatedHighlights: Lyon dossier of the Gottschalk predestination controversy remains largely untranslated

name: Fulbertus Carnotensis
pdTranslations: Hymn translations in 19th-c. hymnals (e.g., 'Ye Choirs of New Jerusalem' in Campbell's Hymns and Anthems 1850)
modernTranslations: The Letters and Poems of Fulbert of Chartres (ed./trans. Frederic Behrends, Oxford Medieval Texts 1976)
untranslatedHighlights: None - comprehensive translation available

name: Gerbertus Auriliacensis
modernTranslations: Letters with English translations in Epistolae database (epistolae.ctl.columbia.edu)
untranslatedHighlights: Mathematical/scientific treatises may lack modern English translations

name: Berno Augiae Divitis
modernTranslations: The Prologus in tonarium of Bern of Reichenau: A Translation (in Greek and Latin Music Theory, Cambridge)
untranslatedHighlights: Other works (liturgical/theological treatises, letters, vitae) among his 13 PL works may lack English translations

name: Joannes Bezuensis
modernTranslations: None located; modern scholarly edition The Cartulary-Chronicle of St-Pierre of Beze (ed. Constance Brittain Bouchard, Medieval Academy/University of Toronto Press 2019) exists but no English translation identified
untranslatedHighlights: Chronicon Besuense (chronicle of Beze Abbey by the monk Jean, d. 1120) remains untranslated

name: Auctor incertus (Maximus Taurinensis?)
modernTranslations: Genuine Maximus sermons translated in The Sermons of St. Maximus of Turin (trans. Boniface Ramsey, ACW 50, 1989); dubious/spurious PL items likely fall outside that corpus
untranslatedHighlights: Attribution unclear - pseudo-Maximus material marked incertus

name: Bandinus
modernTranslations: None located
untranslatedHighlights: Commentary/abridgement of Peter Lombard's Sentences (~1170) remains in Latin

name: Auctor incertus (Bernardus Claraevallensis?)
pdTranslations: Some pseudo-Bernard devotional works circulated in old vernacular/devotional translations (e.g., medieval Italian versions of Meditationes piissimae)
modernTranslations: Genuine Bernard comprehensively translated (Cistercian Fathers series); pseudo-Bernard PL 184 items (e.g., Meditationes piissimae de cognitione humanae conditionis) largely lack modern English translations
untranslatedHighlights: 11 works of uncertain attribution; Meditationes piissimae (PL 184:485-508) - hugely popular medieval devotional compilation - no modern English translation identified
